title: API reference
summary: The composed OpenAPI 3.1 surface: fence flow, Quality, Guard, Bus and operator endpoints.
text: The authoritative contract is the composed application's /openapi.json when documentation is enabled. This site highlights stable high-value surfaces and avoids hardcoding an endpoint count that can drift between release candidates. # Fence flow Method Path Purpose POST /v1/fence/submit Quality → Guard → durable Bus → completion audit # Quality Method Path Purpose GET /v1/quality/controls List admission/control metadata POST /v1/quality/evaluate Run admission evaluator GET /v1/quality/registry Registry summary POST /v1/quality/deep/plan Plan Deep Quality 2.0 evaluation/evidence # Guard Guard is mounted under /guard/v1/* with resources for decisions, capabilities, approvals, policies, tools/executions, artifacts, audit, protocols, tenant lifecycle, workload identity and more. # Bus Bus is mounted under /bus/v1/* with durable handoff, claim/ack, references, routing, protocol/TCK, evaluation and integration surfaces. # API discovery Generate clients and schemas from the live composed /openapi.json ; use the Bus TCK rather than OpenAPI alone for cross-language wire compatibility.

title: Architecture
summary: How Quality, Guard, and Bus compose into one FastAPI control plane with one identity, database, audit chain, and telemetry pipeline.
text:
AIFENCE is one FastAPI application built by one factory. It owns the shared foundation and then invites each installed subsystem to mount itself. text Copy ┌───────────────── aifence.app.create_app() ──────────────────┐
        │ middleware · error envelope · health · metrics · OpenAPI    │
        │ lifespan (bridged) · circuit breakers · identity            │
        └──────┬──────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────┘
               │ register()       │ register()        │ register()
        ┌──────▼─────┐     ┌──────▼──────┐     ┌──────▼──────┐
        │  quality   │────▶│    guard    │────▶│     bus     │
        │  (gate)    │     │ enforcement │     │  transport  │
        └────────────┘     └─────────────┘     └─────────────┘
               └──────────────── aifence.core ───────────────┘
          config · db (one Base/engine) · errors · middleware
                   metrics · telemetry · env helpers # Why a shared core rather than a single monolith The tiers share FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, Alembic, pydantic, cryptography and Prometheus, but their domain configuration and models are distinct. aifence.core owns only the cross-cutting infrastructure every tier uses, while each subsystem keeps its own settings, models and routers. # The composition seam aifence.subsystems defines a register(app, ctx) protocol and discovers installed subsystems in flow order (quality → guard → bus). create_app never imports a subsystem directly. subsystems can be added or replaced without changing the factory; the application runs with any subset installed; each subsystem mounts its own router and wires workers into the shared lifespan; SubsystemContext hands each subsystem the shared settings, engine and session factory. # Mounted sub-applications Guard and Bus are mounted as FastAPI sub-applications at /guard and /bus . They keep their proven internals and router-level authentication while sharing the core engine, declarative Base , and metrics registry. # Lifespans are bridged Starlette does not run a mounted application's lifespan. create_app enters every mounted lifespan through an AsyncExitStack , so HTTP clients, workers and storage clients start and stop as one unit. # OpenAPI is combined Sub-app paths would otherwise live only under their mounted OpenAPI documents. The factory folds them into the root document, rebasing paths and namespacing component schemas to avoid collisions. # Native routers Quality, the Fence flow and the operator console are composed directly onto the root application and are explicitly bound to the same identity model. # One database, one migration history Every subsystem declares its models against aifence.core.db.Base , so one Alembic history builds the entire schema and one connection pool serves every tier. A migration/model drift test prevents undeclared schema changes. # Data flow Quality scores the artifact and emits a quality decision. Guard compiles baseline + tenant policy into an enforcement plan and exact-action capability. Bus durably persists the vetted payload as a claimable handoff, then optionally fans out to a broker. Every step shares the request id, audit chain and telemetry established by the core.

title: Benchmarks & adversarial evaluation
summary: Measured attack detection, false positives, approval friction, behavioral analysis, and CI regression gates.
text:
A detection system is described honestly by two numbers together: how much hostile behavior it catches, and how much legitimate work it breaks. Either alone is marketing. AIFENCE records both and provides a command that reproduces the evaluation. bash Copy aifence-redteam                         # baseline
aifence-redteam --behavioural analysis # cross-tier detector
aifence-redteam --compare               # both + delta # Why traces rather than requests A compromised or drifting agent rarely reveals itself in one request. Scope creeps, claims contradict earlier observations, and output quality decays. The evaluation unit is therefore a multi-turn trace : a sequence of turns by one agent executed against an accumulating observation window. Every attack trace begins with plausible behavior and degrades. An attack that looks malicious on turn one measures little about trajectory-aware controls. # Benign traces are mandatory A detector that refuses everything can claim 100% detection. The suite therefore includes legitimate work near the boundary — real deletes, customer PII, outbound calls, and documents discussing credentials/prompt injection without containing an attack. # Metrics Metric Meaning Detection rate Attack traces stopped by any means, including the default hold. Specific detection Attack traces stopped because a detector fired — the honest detector number. False-positive rate Benign traces hard-refused. Hold rate Benign traces held for human approval: friction, not refusal. # Current measured regression suite Measured on 18 traces: 11 attack + 7 benign . Metric Baseline Behavioral analysis Detection rate 90.9% 100.0% Specific detection 81.8% 90.9% False-positive rate 0.0% 0.0% Hold rate 71.4% 71.4% The 71.4% hold rate is the main operational finding for the strict baseline: most production writes need a human. That is deliberate fail-closed behavior, but it is also measurable friction. Important limitation: 18 traces is a useful regression suite and far too small to treat the percentages as population-level safety claims. The purpose is reproducibility and regression detection, not a universal guarantee. # Policy profiles With behavioral analysis enabled, the measured policy profiles are: Metric Strict Balanced Detection rate 100.0% 100.0% Specific detection 100.0% 100.0% False-positive rate 0.0% 0.0% Held for approval 71.4% 14.3% Balanced matches strict on the measured security outcomes while cutting approval friction from 71.4% to 14.3% — an 80% relative reduction in held benign traces. This depends on behavioral analysis. Without it, Balanced misses an indirect prompt-injection trace carrying an innocuous payload — the kind of case Strict can stop only through blanket default hold rather than specific detection. # Cross-tier behavioral detector The detector emits integrity.behavioral_drift on a deliberately small signal set: Persistent ungrounded assertion — repeated grounding lapses that accumulate across turns. Sustained intent escalation — operation severity rising across a run. Untrusted influence — a state change following attacker-controllable external content. Reading untrusted content alone is not flagged; acting afterward is the signal. # Regression gate bash Copy aifence-redteam --behavioural analysis \
  --max-false-positive-rate 0 \
  --min-detection-rate 100 CI also asserts that the baseline still misses at least one scenario. A suite the current implementation passes trivially demonstrates only that the suite is too easy. # Extending the suite Keep attack scenarios inside approved scope long enough to exercise the detector instead of immediately tripping coarse scope enforcement. Keep benign scenarios realistic and close to trigger conditions, or the false-positive rate becomes meaningless.

title: Bus protocol
summary: Cross-language semantic handoff compatibility is governed by aifence/0.2, wire version 2, and a shared conformance kit.
text: # Protocol identity The Bus implementation version and wire protocol are separate contracts. Current protocol identity is aifence/0.2 with wire version 2 . # Compatibility rules Every packet is validated as wire v2 before expansion. Canonical JSON, canonical MessagePack and SHA-256 digests must match shared vectors. Invalid vectors must be rejected. Python, JavaScript and Go consume the same central TCK vectors. Adapter-local standalone copies must remain byte-identical to the central vectors. # Change rule Protocol changes require a new protocol/wire version or an explicitly backward-compatible TCK change. Bumping the Bus implementation package alone does not redefine wire compatibility. bash Copy python -m aifence.bus.conformance --fuzz

title: Bus tier
summary: The semantic communication runtime — durable handoffs, content-addressed references, learned patterns, and minimum-sufficient state.
text:
The Bus tier is the semantic communication runtime: durable tenant-scoped handoffs, content-addressed references, minimum-sufficient state and protocol-conformant cross-language transport. # Durable delivery text Copy handoff ──▶ pending ──▶ claimed ──▶ acknowledged
                          │
                          └─▶ lease expiry ──▶ claimable again A handoff is committed before it is represented as delivered. Receiver knowledge advances after acknowledgement, so claimed-but-unacked work remains recoverable. # Tenant isolation The composed fence uses tenant-specific Bus workspaces. A receiving agent cannot claim another tenant's fence handoff merely by knowing the receiver name or message ID. # Semantic state Bus preserves minimum-sufficient state rather than replaying entire conversations. High-risk semantics—negation, amounts, identities, authorization, deadlines, environment markers, instructions and constraints—take the strict preservation path. # Content-addressed references Stored content uses SHA-256 identity while authorization/lifetime remain separate grants. Identical bytes can deduplicate without sharing authorization. # Broker transports Backend Mechanism Role none No fan-out Default memory In-process Development/tests redis Redis Stream Optional accelerator kafka Topic keyed by receiver Optional accelerator rabbitmq Durable topic exchange Optional accelerator Broker publication follows the durable commit and carries routing identity rather than semantic content. The database-backed Bus remains source of truth. # Protocol and conformance Bus uses aifence/0.2 , wire version 2 . Canonical JSON/MessagePack digests and valid/invalid behavior are governed by the shared TCK consumed by Python, JavaScript and Go. Read the Bus protocol contract →

title: Configuration
summary: The shared AIFENCE_ environment surface, resilience budgets, multi-region settings, policy profiles, and subsystem ownership.
text: Configuration is read from the environment (and optionally .env ). Every current variable uses the AIFENCE_ prefix. Invalid production configuration is rejected at startup and validation reports every unmet requirement at once. # Core Variable Default Purpose AIFENCE_ENVIRONMENT development development / test / staging / production . AIFENCE_RUNTIME_ROLE control-plane Runtime role. AIFENCE_LOG_LEVEL INFO Root log level. AIFENCE_BIND_HOST 0.0.0.0 Bind host. AIFENCE_BIND_PORT 8080 Bind port. AIFENCE_PUBLIC_BASE_URL http://localhost:8080 Advertised OpenAPI base URL. AIFENCE_DOCS_ENABLED true Expose docs/OpenAPI. AIFENCE_MAX_REQUEST_BYTES 2097152 Global request body ceiling. # Persistence Variable Default Purpose AIFENCE_DATABASE_URL sqlite+pysqlite:///./aifence.db SQLAlchemy URL. AIFENCE_DB_POOL_SIZE 20 Pool size (non-SQLite). AIFENCE_DB_MAX_OVERFLOW 20 Pool overflow. AIFENCE_AUTO_CREATE_SCHEMA true Dev schema creation; use Alembic in production. # Fence flow resilience Variable Default Purpose AIFENCE_FLOW_QUALITY_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 5.0 Quality latency budget. AIFENCE_FLOW_GUARD_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 5.0 Guard latency budget. AIFENCE_FLOW_BUS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS 10.0 Bus latency budget. AIFENCE_FLOW_FAILURE_THRESHOLD 5 Failures before breaker trip. AIFENCE_FLOW_RECOVERY_SECONDS 30.0 Recovery probe window. AIFENCE_FLOW_FAIL_OPEN_TIERS empty Advisory tiers permitted to fail open. Only Quality and Bus. Guard cannot be made fail-open. Naming it is rejected at startup. # Multi-region and transport Variable Default Purpose AIFENCE_REGION empty Region identifier. AIFENCE_REGION_ROLE active active owns writes/workers; standby serves reads. AIFENCE_BUS_TRANSPORT none none , memory , redis , kafka , rabbitmq . AIFENCE_BUS_TRANSPORT_URL empty Broker URL. AIFENCE_BUS_TRANSPORT_TOPIC aifence.handoffs Stream/topic/exchange name. # Policy profiles AIFENCE_GUARD_POLICY_FILE selects the policy document. Two measured profiles ship: strict and balanced . Balanced is designed to reduce approval friction while preserving the evaluated detection behavior when behavioral analysis is enabled. # Secrets For secret-backed variables, <NAME>_FILE can point to a mounted secret file. This lets containers and Helm consume secrets without placing them in pod specs.

title: Deployment
summary: Migrations, containers, Helm, production hardening, multi-region active/standby topology, and broker transports.
text:
# Database migrations Production should run with AIFENCE_AUTO_CREATE_SCHEMA=false ; Alembic is the only thing that creates tables. bash Copy alembic upgrade head A test asserts migrations produce the declared models and the history has one head, preventing silent schema drift. # Container bash Copy docker compose up --build      # PostgreSQL + the control plane The image runs as a non-root user and serves aifence-api on port 8080. # Helm The chart lives under deploy/helm/aifence and deploys the control plane plus dispatcher, lifecycle and audit-anchor worker roles, migration job, network policy, HPA, PDB and ingress. bash Copy helm upgrade --install aifence deploy/helm/aifence -f my-values.yaml # Production validation Production validation rejects unsafe persistence, schema auto-create, interactive docs, wildcard hosts/CORS, non-HTTPS public origins, unsafe in-memory transport, weak private-metrics configuration, and missing hardened identity/signing/evidence controls required by the selected runtime role. # Multi-region topology Exactly one region is active : it owns the writable database and durable workers. Other regions are standby : they can serve the control plane from replicas and remain warm for promotion. yaml Copy # active
region: { name: eu-west-1, role: active }
# standby
region: { name: us-east-1, role: standby } Three independent guardrails prevent a standby from behaving like the active region: Startup validation refuses standby + durable worker role. The Helm chart does not render durable workers/migration outside the active region. Readiness publishes accepts_writes , so a global load balancer sends writes only to active. # Bus transports bash Copy AIFENCE_BUS_TRANSPORT=redis
AIFENCE_BUS_TRANSPORT_URL=redis://redis:6379/0
AIFENCE_BUS_TRANSPORT_TOPIC=aifence.handoffs Publication happens after the durable commit and carries routing identity rather than semantic content. # Health and observability Path Purpose /health/live Liveness probe. /health/ready Readiness; reports region and accepts_writes . /metrics Private-by-default Prometheus scrape target. Set AIFENCE_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT to enable OpenTelemetry tracing.

title: Failure semantics
summary: Failure behavior is part of the AIFENCE security contract, not an incidental runtime detail.
text: # Default behavior Component / failure Default Reason Quality admission timeout/unavailable Fail closed Unvetted artifacts do not silently proceed Guard timeout/unavailable/policy error Always fail closed Authorization never degrades into authorization-by-absence Bus persistence/handoff failure Fail closed A receipt cannot claim a handoff that was not committed Fence audit append failure Fail closed A governed decision without its audit event is incomplete Optional telemetry exporter failure Degraded Telemetry transport is not an authorization dependency Optional broker fan-out failure Degraded / retry Database-backed Bus remains source of truth Database unavailable Fail closed Identity, policy, audit and handoff state are unavailable Signing/KMS unavailable Fail closed where signed evidence is required Unsigned evidence cannot be represented as verified Deep Quality runtime unavailable Admission remains available Deep evaluation is explicit, not an admission dependency # Narrow fail-open exception Only quality and bus may be deliberately named as advisory fence tiers. guard is rejected if present in AIFENCE_FLOW_FAIL_OPEN_TIERS . # Receipt rule A handed_off receipt means admission passed, Guard permitted the action, the Bus handoff was durably created, and the fence-completion audit event was appended. Optional telemetry export and broker propagation are not part of that transactional success claim.

title: Fence flow
summary: The three tiers as one governed pipeline, with short-circuiting, resilience budgets, and one truthful receipt.

title: Getting started
summary: Install AIFENCE, mint a key, and run an artifact through the complete Quality → Guard → Bus fence.
text:
# Install AIFENCE targets Python 3.12+. Create an isolated environment and install the repository. bash Copy python -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate              # Windows: .venv\Scripts\activate
python -m pip install -e ".[dev]" # Prove the complete fence locally The fastest supported proof is the real composed demo. It creates an isolated database, a tenant/API key, runs Quality → Guard → Bus , claims the durable handoff as the receiver, and exits non-zero if the lifecycle is incomplete. bash Copy aifence demo # Diagnose your runtime Validate resolved configuration, application/database construction, the packaged Quality registry and Bus protocol resources before running a persistent service. bash Copy aifence doctor # Run the service Start the composed API, then bootstrap the first administrative identity in another terminal. bash Copy aifence serve

# second terminal
aifence bootstrap --tenant-name acme The API key is shown once. Store it immediately, then use it for governed endpoints. # Submit through the complete fence bash Copy export AIFENCE_API_KEY='replace-with-bootstrap-token'
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/fence/submit \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $AIFENCE_API_KEY" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "artifact":"# Deployment note\n\nThe candidate passed the required validation and rollback ownership is documented.",
    "content_type":"text/markdown",
    "receiver":"release-agent",
    "action":{"operation":"read"},
    "risk_score":10
  }' A successful receipt identifies the Quality mode/profile, Guard matched rule/reason codes, tenant-scoped Bus workspace/message, request ID and signed audit event. # Production note Development defaults favor local startup. Production validation rejects SQLite, schema auto-create, interactive docs, wildcard hosts/CORS, unsafe in-memory transport, non-HTTPS public origins and weak private-metrics configuration. Run aifence doctor in the intended production environment before deployment.

title: Guard tier
summary: The enforcement plane — decides and enforces what an agent is permitted to do.
text:
Guard is the mandatory enforcement plane. It evaluates sensitive actions outside the agent process; required controls must compile into an executable plan or the operation fails closed. # Decision pipeline text Copy DecisionRequest
   │
   ├─▶ detectors / content classification
   ├─▶ risk scoring
   ├─▶ policy engine
   ▼
outcome + constraints + matched rule + reason codes
   ▼
enforcement plan → exact-action capability # Outcomes Outcome Meaning allow Proceed unchanged allow_with_limits Proceed under constraints redact_or_transform Proceed only after transformation require_approval Hold for human decision deny Refuse quarantine_and_terminate Refuse, isolate artifact and end run # Decision explainability Decisions expose stable GUARD_* reason codes together with the exact matched policy rule and decision context. Operators can answer who requested an operation, on which resource/tenant, which policy matched, and why it was allowed or denied without parsing free-form prose. # Capability tokens An allow decision does not itself perform an action. Guard issues an exact-action capability bound to tool, operation, resource and arguments, with TTL and maximum-use limits. # Identity and evidence API keys are scoped and tenant-bound; PostgreSQL row-level security provides tenant isolation. Decisions produce signed receipts and hash-chained audit events/checkpoints that can be anchored independently. # Production posture Production startup validation enforces hardened persistence, identity, signing/KMS, evidence, audit anchoring, egress and origin/metrics settings. Guard cannot be configured fail-open.

title: Operations
summary: Run the fence with operator status, health probes, Prometheus metrics, OpenTelemetry traces, and explicit degradation signals.
text: # Operator console GET /v1/console/ renders operator state; GET /v1/console/status returns JSON. The view ties durable handoffs, approvals, subsystem state, Quality registry and transport configuration together. # Health probes Path Use /health/live Process liveness /health/ready Readiness, region and accepts_writes # Canonical fence telemetry One request ID spans Quality, Guard, Bus, logs/traces and the completion audit. Metric Purpose aifence_fence_stage_calls_total{tier,result,breaker_state} Per-tier outcome/circuit state aifence_fence_stage_duration_seconds{tier} Per-tier latency aifence_fence_outcomes_total{outcome,allowed} Final fence outcomes # Metrics access /metrics is private by default. Production private metrics require a bearer token of at least 32 bytes unless public metrics are deliberately enabled. # Tracing AIFENCE_OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT enables OpenTelemetry export. Content payloads are not placed into span attributes; exporter failure must not mutate policy outcomes. # Audit linkage Every completed fence flow appends fence.completed . The receipt exposes audit event ID, sequence, event hash and signing key ID so an operator can reconstruct request → admission → Guard → Bus → audit .

title: Quality modes
summary: Admission is the bounded synchronous gate; Deep Quality 2.0 plans the broader family-native evaluation and evidence requirements.
text: # Admission POST /v1/fence/submit and POST /v1/quality/evaluate use the deterministic admission evaluator. It answers whether an artifact is sufficiently complete and structurally sound to enter the governed action path. Response field Meaning mode admission profile The admission profile used evaluator_version The evaluator version findings[] Stable ID, severity, evidence and remediation # Deep Quality 2.0 The repository's quality/ source pack is the broader Quality 2.0 runtime. POST /v1/quality/deep/plan bridges to the built runtime and returns the family-native evaluation/evidence plan. It is explicit and is not silently run for every fence submission. # Client contract Clients should branch on explicit mode/profile metadata. An admission pass must not be represented as proof that the entire 1,000-control Quality corpus executed.

title: Quality tier
summary: Scores AI-generated artifacts against production quality controls before sensitive enforcement or transport runs.
text:
The Quality tier is the first gate in the composed fence. A failed admission artifact is stopped before Guard evaluates the action. # Two explicit modes Admission is the fast deterministic synchronous gate used by /v1/fence/submit and /v1/quality/evaluate . Deep Quality 2.0 is the broader family-native runtime exposed explicitly through /v1/quality/deep/plan . Read the Quality modes contract → # Architecture text Copy quality/source/control_registry.csv   1,000 canonical controls
        │
        ├── packaged registry snapshot ──▶ admission evaluator
        │
        └── deterministic build ─────────▶ Deep Quality 2.0 runtime # Admission findings Admission findings are machine-readable and stable enough for clients and regression tooling: identifier, severity, evidence, remediation, evaluator version and profile. Example ID Purpose AQ-COMPLETE-001 Completeness failure AQ-TEMPLATE-001 Unresolved template/placeholder signal AQ-GROUNDING-001 Grounding evidence failure # Admission checks Check Role What it catches completeness Mandatory Empty artifact anti_template Mandatory TODO/TBD/PLACEHOLDER/Lorem ipsum answerability Scored Too little useful substance link_integrity Scored Empty/placeholder markup links structure Scored Missing markup structure json_validity Mandatory for JSON Non-parsing JSON schema_conformance Mandatory when supplied Contract violations grounding Conditional Numeric claims absent from supplied sources # API Endpoint Purpose GET /v1/quality/registry Registry summary GET /v1/quality/controls List/filter controls POST /v1/quality/evaluate Run admission POST /v1/quality/deep/plan Plan Deep Quality 2.0 evaluation/evidence

title: SDKs
summary: Python, TypeScript and Go clients, plus agent-framework enforcement hooks.
text:
Official SDKs are versioned on the 1.0.0rc5 compatibility line and live under sdks/ . Language Path Package / module Python sdks/python aifence-client / aifence_client TypeScript sdks/typescript @aifence/client Go sdks/go github.com/aifence/aifence-go # Guard client base URL The current SDK client surface is Guard-first: point the client at the Guard mount, then use typed/structured decision, capability, policy, approval and audit methods. python Copy from aifence_client import AifenceClient

client = AifenceClient(
    "https://aifence.example.com/guard",
    api_key="replace-with-secret-manager-value",
)
decision = client.decide({...}) # Full composed fence The composed transaction is rooted at POST /v1/fence/submit . Use the root API contract shown in Getting Started for the full Quality → Guard → Bus → audit path. Compatibility note: the SDKs expose a submitFence / submit_fence / SubmitFence method in this source tree, but a client configured with a /guard base URL must not be assumed to resolve that root endpoint correctly. Treat the root fence endpoint as the canonical contract until that URL split is normalized in the SDK implementation. # Client behavior Clients require HTTPS, use bounded timeouts/retries, do not follow redirects, cap response sizes, and expose AIFENCE structured errors. Python additionally supports mTLS.

title: Security model
summary: Shared identity, content classification, evidence, controlled egress, and an intentionally fail-closed posture.
text: # One identity model The fence, Quality endpoints, operator console and Guard surfaces use Guard-backed identity rather than parallel weaker credentials. Surface Authentication posture /health/live , /health/ready Probe endpoints /metrics Private by default; production private metrics require a strong bearer token unless explicitly made public /v1/fence/submit API key with decision-write authority /v1/quality/* API key /v1/console/* API key with read authority /guard/* Guard router-level authentication # Fail-closed posture Guard is always fail closed. Unknown policy constraints fail closed. Database/audit/signing failures fail closed where they are part of the governed contract. Standby regions cannot silently assume durable-worker responsibility. Unsafe production configuration is rejected at startup. Read exact failure semantics → # Tenant and wire boundaries Fence Bus workspaces are tenant-specific, idempotency is bound to sender/receiver/payload digest, and wire v2 is validated against a frozen TCK before semantic expansion. # Evidence Fence completion appends a tamper-evident fence.completed audit event containing artifact digest—not artifact contents—plus Quality, Guard and Bus decision metadata. # Network controls Outbound calls use HTTPS-only destinations, canonical path confinement, DNS revalidation/IP pinning, preserved TLS identity, no redirect following, controlled egress and bounded response sizes. # Threat model The repository maps priority threats to explicit controls and regression/conformance coverage. Read the threat model →

title: Supply chain
summary: Release integrity certifies built artifacts, protocol fixtures, generated Quality outputs, dependencies, and clean-install behavior.
text: # Required release path Lint, strict type-check and Python tests with enforced coverage. Red-team, security, architecture, invariant and release-consistency gates. Build/test canonical Quality runtime from source. Build/test Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs and required adapters. Run Bus TCK across required implementations. Build Python wheel and source archive. Verify package integrity and smoke/conformance-test the clean wheel. Generate vulnerability and SBOM artifacts. Publish checksums/provenance; sign artifacts/images where supported. # Generated Quality tree quality/build/ is generated output, not source-of-truth. quality/source/ plus deterministic tooling reconstructs it. The small control-registry snapshot shipped in the wheel is checked byte-for-byte against canonical source. # Dependency policy Dependency changes should pass the complete release gate, not merely an individual package build. Production dependencies remain explicitly bounded or pinned where reproducibility/signature review requires it.

title: Threat model
summary: Trust boundaries and regression-backed controls for unauthorized, unaudited, cross-tenant, or tampered agent actions and handoffs.
text: # Security objective AIFENCE prevents an AI agent or integration from converting untrusted/generated work into an unauthorized or unaudited downstream action, and prevents semantic handoff state from crossing tenant or protocol boundaries without enforcement. # Trust boundaries Caller → composed API: API keys/mTLS establish identity; request-size and host/origin controls constrain ingress. Quality → Guard: admission quality never grants authority; Guard independently evaluates action, principal, environment and risk. Guard → Bus: only permitted Guard outcomes can create a fence handoff. Tenant → tenant: Bus workspaces and identity state are tenant-scoped. Wire → implementation: Bus wire v2 is validated against the frozen protocol/TCK contract. Runtime → evidence: audit events are hash-chained and signed without copying artifact contents into fence-completion events. # Priority threats Threat Primary control Coverage Anonymous fence use Shared Guard-backed identity Fence conformance Cross-tenant message access Tenant-specific Bus workspace Fence conformance Policy bypass / confused deputy Mandatory fail-closed Guard stage Integration + red-team Ambiguous denial handling Stable Guard reason codes + matched rule Guard policy/service tests Low-quality placeholder work Stable Admission Quality findings Quality/fence tests Idempotency replay with changed content Sender/receiver/payload digest binding Bus + conformance Malformed/tampered semantic wire Frozen schema + TCK + mutation suite Bus conformance Audit tampering Per-tenant hash chain + signatures/checkpoints Audit + fence conformance Oversized request abuse Streaming-aware request limiter Core/integration Unsafe production defaults Startup validation Configuration tests Secret leakage through metrics Private metrics + bearer auth Core application tests Source/package drift Release/registry/package gates CI release checks # Residual risk AIFENCE cannot prove that external tools, models or downstream agents behave correctly after authorized execution. Operators still need to protect infrastructure credentials, configure tenant policy correctly, secure database/KMS infrastructure, and evaluate model-specific prompt/tool risks.

title: Version model
summary: Independent platform, subsystem, SDK, and protocol versions without implying identical compatibility semantics.
text: # Current inventory Surface Current version Compatibility meaning AIFENCE platform 0.1.0 Monorepo/application release version Guard implementation 1.0.0rc5 Guard API and implementation release Bus implementation 0.2.7 Semantic Bus implementation release Quality runtime 2.0.0 Canonical Quality source/runtime release Official SDK line 1.0.0rc5 Python/TypeScript client compatibility line Bus protocol aifence/0.2 Cross-language semantic handoff protocol Bus wire version 2 Frozen wire-envelope schema version # Source of truth The executable version inventory lives in src/aifence/versions.py . Protocol compatibility is proven by TCK vectors rather than inferred from implementation package numbers. bash Copy aifence version # Release rule A platform release may contain different component versions. A release is valid only when CI proves required SDKs/adapters conform to the protocol and package metadata matches the central inventory.
